tasks.title: Implement Responsive Design and Cross-Browser Compatibility
tasks.description: Implement full website responsiveness for correct display on mobile devices, tablets, and desktops, including adapting layouts, images, fonts, and controls, and ensuring cross-browser compatibility.
tasks.details: 1. **Viewport Configuration:** Set the viewport meta tag in the HTML to control scaling and dimensions on different devices. 2. **CSS Media Queries:** Implement CSS media queries to apply different styles based on screen size and device type. Define breakpoints for mobile, tablet, and desktop. 3. **Flexible Layouts:** Use flexible CSS layouts such as Flexbox or Grid to create layouts that adapt to different screen sizes. 4. **Image Optimization:** Optimize images for different screen resolutions using the `` element or `srcset` attribute in `` tags. Use responsive image techniques to load appropriate image sizes based on the device. 5. **Font Scaling:** Use relative units (em, rem, vw, vh) for font sizes to ensure text scales appropriately on different devices. 6. **Touch-Friendly Controls:** Ensure that interactive elements (buttons, links, forms) are touch-friendly by providing sufficient spacing and using appropriate sizes. 7. **Cross-Browser Testing:** Test the website on multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) and devices to ensure compatibility. Use browser developer tools to identify and fix any layout or rendering issues. 8. **Accessibility:** Ensure the responsive design is accessible by following accessibility guidelines (WCAG). Use semantic HTML and provide alternative text for images.
tasks.testStrategy:
1.  **Manual Testing:** Manually test the website on different devices (mobile phones, tablets, desktops) and browsers to verify that the layout, images, fonts, and controls are displayed correctly.
2.  **Browser Developer Tools:** Use browser developer tools (e.g., Chrome DevTools) to simulate different screen sizes and device types. Inspect the CSS and HTML to ensure that the correct styles are being applied.
3.  **Automated Testing:** Use automated testing tools (e.g., Selenium, Cypress) to test the responsive design. Write tests to verify that the layout adapts correctly to different screen sizes and that all elements are displayed as expected.
4.  **Cross-Browser Testing Tools:** Use cross-browser testing tools (e.g., BrowserStack, Sauce Labs) to test the website on different browsers and operating systems.
5.  **Performance Testing:** Use performance testing tools (e.g., Google PageSpeed Insights, Lighthouse) to measure the performance of the responsive design. Optimize images and CSS to improve loading times on mobile devices.

subtasks.title: Implement Viewport Configuration and Initial CSS Media Queries
subtasks.description: Set the viewport meta tag in the HTML and implement basic CSS media queries for mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints.
subtasks.details: Configure the viewport meta tag to control scaling and dimensions. Define initial breakpoints in CSS using media queries for common device sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop).
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify the viewport meta tag is correctly set in the HTML. Manually resize the browser window to trigger different media queries and confirm that basic styles are applied correctly at each breakpoint.

subtasks.title: Develop Flexible Layouts with Flexbox or Grid
subtasks.description: Implement flexible CSS layouts using Flexbox or Grid to ensure content adapts to different screen sizes.
subtasks.details: Choose either Flexbox or Grid (or a combination) to create flexible layouts for key website sections. Ensure that elements reflow and resize appropriately as the screen size changes.
subtasks.testStrategy: Resize the browser window and inspect the layout to ensure elements reflow and resize correctly. Test on different devices (mobile, tablet, desktop) to verify layout responsiveness.

subtasks.title: Optimize Images for Different Screen Resolutions
subtasks.description: Optimize images using the `` element or `srcset` attribute in `` tags to load appropriate image sizes based on the device.
subtasks.details: Implement responsive image techniques using the `<picture>` element or `srcset` attribute. Create multiple image sizes for different screen resolutions and pixel densities. Optimize image file sizes to improve loading times.
subtasks.testStrategy: Use browser developer tools to inspect the images being loaded on different devices and screen sizes. Verify that the appropriate image size is being loaded for each device. Measure image loading times to ensure optimization is effective.

subtasks.title: Implement Font Scaling and Touch-Friendly Controls
subtasks.description: Use relative units for font sizes and ensure interactive elements are touch-friendly.
subtasks.details: Use relative units (em, rem, vw, vh) for font sizes to ensure text scales appropriately. Increase the size and spacing of interactive elements (buttons, links, forms) to make them touch-friendly.
subtasks.testStrategy: Resize the browser window and verify that font sizes scale appropriately. Test interactive elements on touch devices to ensure they are easy to tap and use.

subtasks.description: Test the website on multiple browsers and devices, and conduct an accessibility audit to ensure compliance with WCAG guidelines.
subtasks.details: Test the website on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge on different devices (mobile, tablet, desktop). Use browser developer tools to identify and fix any layout or rendering issues. Conduct an accessibility audit using tools like WAVE or Axe to identify and fix accessibility issues. Ensure semantic HTML is used and alternative text is provided for images.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manually test the website on different browsers and devices. Use browser developer tools to identify and fix layout and rendering issues. Run an accessibility audit using automated tools and manually verify accessibility guidelines are followed.
